text:
maria: hey team, trying to run a long nsys capture (30s) for kv-cache stress test but results look biased — kernel timeline shows big gaps and a handful of hot kernels repeated. thinking sampling window + nvtx bracketting is skewing what we see. command I'm using:

```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --sample=cpu --capture-range=nvtx --capture-range-end=END --force-overwrite -o kv-stress.qdrep --duration=30s ./run_kv_stress.sh
```

any quick sanity checks? 

kevin: first thought: 30s is long for a single bracket. NVTX capture-range will only include time between markers, but sampling still picks a subset. try shorter bracketed segments (3-5s) repeated and then merge traces. also warmup matters — make sure KV prefetch/warmup is outside the bracket. :mag_right:

maria: good call, warmup might be inside the range — I put a prep loop in the script. will move it out. how do you merge traces?

sara: you can do iterative captures and stitch on the timeline in Nsight GUI, or use `nsys export` to flatten and combine metrics. practical approach: capture N short windows with NVTX start/stop around the interesting region, toggle `--sample=none` for long-running but high-overhead traces, and `--sample=cpu` for short detail runs. 

chris: another tip: OSRT sampling gives lower overhead for runtime events but it's noisy for small kernels. If kernel durations are microsecond-scale, sampling will miss them unless you bracket tightly. For kernel-level accuracy use `--trace=cuda` with explicit start/end NVTX and `--capture-range-cpu` (or `--capture-range=nvtx`), then reduce sampling.

maria: ok. still seeing repeated hot kernel (~conv_kern_v2) even after short captures; could that be scheduler-affinity or kernel selection changing later in run? the repeated spikes line up with KV eviction events.

kevin: KV eviction triggers concurrent prefetch -> kernel storm. Two things to try:
- isolate a single request path (no background eviction) to baseline kernel set
- instrument eviction path with NVTX and small CPU timestamps: `nvtxRangePush("evict_start")` / `nvtxRangePop()` so trace shows exact overlap.

infra-bot: deploy-check: staging nodes using driver 510.x vs prod 525.x — driver/kernel differences can change kernel selection heuristics. Confirm driver/CUDA version parity.

maria: good catch @infra-bot — staging was on 510. I'll repro on prod image.

sara: if you suspect sampling bias, run a gpu-trace-only capture for a very short window with `--sample=none` and `--trace=cuda` then use the timeline to capture kernel launch/complete timestamps. Sampling is only for counters — trace=cuda gives exact kernel events. Example quick command I use:

```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx --sample=none --capture-range=nvtx --capture-range-duration=5s -o quick.qdrep ./run_short_case.sh
```

chris: also watch for asynchronous CUDA streams: kernels may not serialize on timeline if you're missing stream correlation markers. OSRT helps, but you need to also annotate host code with nvtx markers at enqueue points. Without that, nsys attributes kernels to threads in odd ways.

maria: that explains some of the weird ordering. I'll add NVTX around enqueue + eviction. last Q: any advice on keeping file sizes reasonable? 30s full trace -> 2-3GB and GUI chokes.

kevin: chunk it. capture many small traces and use sampling for long-run trends. use `--output-filter` to drop uninteresting processes, and `--force-overwrite` to avoid disk bloat. Use `nsys stats` to pre-scan qdrep before opening GUI. Also store metrics-only exports (`nsys export -f sqlite`) for long-term analysis.

maria: awesome, thanks. I'll run: warmup outside bracket; add NVTX to enqueue/evict; short 5s NVTX windows with `--sample=none` + a couple of 2s `--sample=cpu` runs. will post a short qdrep if issues persist. :thumbsup:
